doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Studio work, LA clubs and club dates
summary: He avoided studio work, played Italian jazz clubs in LA, and explains club dates.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah I do occasionally, I get a call to do something special. I wasn’t a studio player and I didn’t really like it, I didn’t like the competition there, I didn’t like the politics of it so I decided to steer clear of it. And there was enough jazz playing. There were a lot of good jazz clubs in those days in Los Angeles. There was Pasquale’s, Dante’s, Alfonso’s, Carmello’s, all Italian joints. They were all Italian places. And they were really good. I mean you’d play there, several of those, several times a week. The only thing with that was they never paid too much so you’d have to do special things to really make some good money. And occasionally a club date. Club dates paid well. But try to steer clear of that too, as I do here. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
Define, for someone who might be watching this, who doesn’t know what club date means.

A club date is a regular job where you play for an audience that doesn’t care what you’re doing. If you’re playing a wedding, nobody cares who the band is. If you’re playing a dance, no one really cares what the band is.
It’s funny when you think about you get paid more on the jobs where people don’t care what you’re doing.
